nodes.description: Independent of its interphase chromatin-remodeling role, SRCAP localizes dynamically to centrosomes, the mitotic spindle, and the midbody during cell division, where it interacts with cytokinesis regulators and promotes their midbody recruitment. SRCAP depletion causes chromosome misalignment, abnormally shaped spindles, chromatin bridges, and failed abscission, which may contribute to developmental growth failure.

nodes.description: Heterozygous nonsense or frameshift variants clustering in exons 33 and 34 of SRCAP produce a C-terminally truncated ATPase subunit lacking the three C-terminal AT-hook DNA-binding motifs while retaining N-terminal Helicase-SANT-Associated ATPase, and CBP-binding domains. In human embryonic cranial neural crest cells, C-terminally truncated SRCAP is largely excluded from the nucleus, exerting a dominant-negative effect on the multiprotein INO80-family SRCAP chromatin remodeling complex.
